about: R1 Frappe 101 as full comic (D-166). Generated from brand-system/r1/r1_comic.py, the same file as the panel script and the preview. Facts: r1-fact-sheet.md, read on frappe.io on 5 Nov 2026. Loaded by patch v1_6.r1_full_comic.

explainers.takeaway: Before you pick software, look at who builds it and how.

panels.caption: The Coffee Company. 11 PM. Three spreadsheets, and they disagree.
panels.thought: One of these sheets is lying. Which one?

panels.left_bubble: The Ethiopian roast? By tomorrow? Consider it done!

panels.caption: Next morning.
panels.left_bubble: Before I trust software with my company: who actually builds it?

panels.right_bubble: Coffee first. It started where you are: a family business stuck with bad software.

panels.caption: His family’s furniture business was stuck with a bad ERP. So Rushabh Mehta, Frappe’s founder, started writing his own.
Its co-founders: Nabin Hait, Mohammad Umair Sayed and Prakash Hodage.
panels.left_bubble: And who runs Frappe now? Managers?

panels.right_bubble: No managers. People pick their work, set their own pay, and vote.
They call themselves a collective. People first, capital second.

panels.left_bubble: No managers? That sounds risky.
panels.right_bubble: Unusual, yes. Don’t take my word for it. It’s all public.

panels.left_bubble: So I check the builders, not only the brochure.
panels.right_bubble: Same test you’d use on a bean supplier.

panels.caption: Across the room, Sara, who runs finance, heard all of it.
panels.thought: Their code is public? So what’s the catch?

explainers.takeaway: You can read, run and change the code. Your system stays yours.

panels.caption: Sara runs finance. She trusts numbers, not brochures.
panels.thought: Nobody gives things away. There’s always a catch.

panels.left_bubble: Frappe lets anyone read its code. Why would anyone do that?

panels.right_bubble: It began as an accident. Now it’s the core of Frappe.

panels.caption: Frappe’s view: open software builds something everyone can use, and never ties its users down.
panels.thought: An accident is not a business plan.

panels.left_bubble: Open how? Can we actually read it?
panels.right_bubble: Yes. ERPNext and the Framework are fully open. Nothing held back.

panels.caption: ERPNext’s code has been public since 2009. On GitHub since 2011.
At the next table: Joseph, who runs tech.
panels.left_bubble: I’ve read their code. Twice. For fun.
Say we want a different partner in a few years. Then what?
panels.right_bubble: Then you move. The code is open, so nobody can lock you in.

panels.left_bubble: And our books come with us.

panels.right_bubble: One catch. Open code still needs good people to set it up and run it.

panels.left_bubble: Which people?
panels.right_bubble: Frappe and its partners. To run it, I’d start with Frappe Cloud.

panels.left_bubble: Fine. Proven, for now.
Open code, fine. But what’s actually in the box?

explainers.takeaway: Frappe makes business apps, developer tools and a cloud, on one stack.

panels.caption: Joseph keeps the laptops, the phones and every sheet that breaks.
panels.thought: Before anyone picks an app, I want the whole map.

panels.left_bubble: So is Frappe one app, or a whole stack?

panels.right_bubble: Business apps, tools for developers, and a cloud. All from one stack.

panels.caption: Also: Learning, Insights, Lending, Raven. For builders: the Framework, Builder, Frappe UI. Under it all: Frappe Cloud.

panels.left_bubble: A CRM? I keep every lead up here!
Hello? Sorry, which cafe wanted the decaf?
Which came first?
panels.right_bubble: The Framework. They built it so they could build ERPNext.

panels.caption: Then their own deployment platform. Then their own UI library.
panels.left_bubble: They built the tools to build the tool.
So stock, leads and complaints could all run on Frappe?
panels.right_bubble: Yes. On Frappe Cloud you choose which apps to install.

panels.left_bubble: So we install everything on day one?
panels.right_bubble: No. Range isn’t fit. Check each app against how you work.

panels.left_bubble: So it’s Frappe all the way down.
Enough about the company. What does the software actually do?
panels.right_bubble: That’s next. First up: buying and selling.
